name: v2026.10.12: Per-tool Python runtimes for PyPI tools, Gradle workspace discovery, and env file find_up
body:
PyPI and pipx tools can now choose their own Python runtime, the workspace graph can read Gradle multi-module builds, and `env._.file` can search parent directories. When mise-versions is having an outage, GitHub lookups now retry on `api.github.com`, and `_.source` scripts no longer pick up `~/.bashrc` when mise is launched from an editor.

## Added

- **Per-tool Python for `pypi:` tools.** Set `python` to a minor series or an exact version, and mise installs that runtime and passes it to uv or pipx for that tool only. The runtime stays private to the tool and does not become your shell's default Python. `mise lock` records the selected Python with the tool, and `mise prune` keeps any runtime that a retained tool environment still uses. You can't combine `python` with `--python`/`-p` in `uvx_args` or `pipx_args`. Tools that don't set `python` behave as before. [#14479](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14479) (@jdx)

  ```toml
  [tools]
  "pypi:black" = { version = "latest", python = "3.12" }
  "pypi:ruff" = { version = "latest", python = "3.12.12" }
  ```

  If you change a tool's `python`, mise installs a new environment instead of reusing the old one. If that install fails, the previous working environment is left untouched. [#14504](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14504) (@jdx)

- **Gradle workspace discovery.** `mise tasks graph` and `mise run --affected` now find projects listed by `include` in `settings.gradle` or `settings.gradle.kts`, using Groovy or Kotlin syntax. Project IDs follow Gradle paths: `:app` becomes `gradle::app`, and the root project is `gradle::`. Literal `project(":lib")` references in a project's top-level `dependencies {}` block become graph edges. mise reads the scripts as text and never runs Gradle. If an `include` is computed or conditional, a `projectDir` isn't a plain `file("...")` literal, or both settings files exist, mise reports an error that points to `[monorepo.projects."gradle:..."]` overrides. Editing the settings script marks every Gradle project as affected. Based on a prototype by @Jarvvski. [#14512](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14512) (@jdx)

- **`find_up` for `env._.file`.** With `find_up = true`, mise looks for a relative path in the current directory and in every parent, so a global config can load each project's `.env` files. Files load from the root down, so values in closer files win. The default is `false`, and the option has no effect on absolute paths. [#14497](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14497) (@jdx)

  ```toml
  # ~/.config/mise/config.toml
  [env]
  _.file = [
    { path = ".env", find_up = true },
    { path = ".env.local", find_up = true },
  ]
  ```

- **Detect git-rewritten files in `watch_files` hooks.** mise sets `MISE_WATCH_FILES_GIT_REWRITTEN=1` when every changed file was last written before git's most recent HEAD move (checkout, pull, rebase). Commits don't count as HEAD moves. Hooks such as format-on-edit can use this to skip files the user didn't edit. `git stash pop`/`apply` don't move HEAD, so mise doesn't detect them. [#14511](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14511) (@jdx)

  ```toml
  [[watch_files]]
  patterns = ["**/*.go"]
  run = '[ -n "$MISE_WATCH_FILES_GIT_REWRITTEN" ] || { IFS=:; hk fix $MISE_WATCH_FILES_MODIFIED; }'
  ```

- **`.tera` sources inferred for dotfile group templates.** A `mode = "template"` entry in `[dotfile_groups]` no longer needs a `source` just to point at a `.tera` file. If the exact path doesn't exist, mise falls back to the same path with `.tera` added. An explicit `source` still takes precedence, and the `.tera` file is not also deployed under its suffixed name. [#14502](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14502) (@jdx)

- **`mise lock` warns about unsupported platforms.** If you name platforms with `lockfile_platforms` or `mise lock --platform`, mise prints a warning for each tool version that has no build for one of them, for example `apko@0.30.0 is not available for windows-x64; it will not install there`. The default platform set still only logs this at debug level, and the exit status is unchanged. [#14500](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14500) (@jdx)

- Registry: added `martin` (`github:maplibre/martin`). [#14488](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14488) (@ivan-ivkovic, @jdx)

## Fixed

- **GitHub lookups survive mise-versions outages.** If mise-versions times out, drops the connection, or returns `429` or `5xx`, mise now retries the lookup on `api.github.com`, using your GitHub token if one is set. This covers releases, tags, repository contents, attestations and `self-update`. A `404`, `403` or empty answer from mise-versions is still trusted and not retried, so normal use doesn't spend GitHub's anonymous rate limit. If both sources fail, the error shows both failures, and a previously cached version list is still used. [#14501](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14501) (@jdx)
- **`_.source` no longer loads `~/.bashrc`.** When mise's stdin was a socket and `SHLVL` was unset, which happens when an editor extension such as the VS Code mise extension starts it, bash sourced `~/.bashrc` before the script. That leaked variables into the environment and could drop the script's `PATH` entries. The script now runs with `--norc`. [#14487](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14487) (@pikeas)
- **Each version entry uses its own options.** When a tool listed several versions, options set only on the first entry leaked into the later ones. For example, `prerelease = true` on a `latest` entry made a separate `"1"` entry resolve to a prerelease. [#14476](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14476) (@JamBalaya56562, @risu729)
- **Project overrides now work when a workspace provider fails.** Previously, if a provider couldn't read its manifest (for example, a malformed `go.work`), `mise tasks graph` and `mise run --affected` failed for the whole repo. Declaring a project in that provider's namespace under `[monorepo.projects]` now replaces the provider's output and clears its error. Providers with no declared projects still fail loudly. [#14508](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14508) (@jdx)

## Documentation

- Explained why `mise activate` keeps shims on `PATH` [#14493](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14493) (@jdx), and clarified the platform-specific mise cache paths for CI [#14506](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14506) (@zeitlinger).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/mise/compare/v2026.10.11...v2026.10.12

## 💚 Sponsor mise

mise is built and maintained by [@jdx](https://github.com/jdx), an open source developer at [**entire.io**](https://entire.io/), the title sponsor of his open source work.

If mise saves you or your team time, please consider becoming an [individual or company sponsor](https://jdx.dev/sponsors.html). Your support funds ongoing development and helps keep mise fast, free, and independent.

name: v2026.10.11: Much faster installs and far fewer GitHub API calls
body:
mise is much faster in this release and calls the GitHub API far less. Version lists, release tags, attestations and other public GitHub metadata now come from mise-versions, so everyday commands like `mise install`, `exec`, shims, `outdated`, `lock` and `self-update` are quicker and users without a GitHub token no longer run into the 60-requests-an-hour limit. Cached version lists are reused for longer, so repeat installs skip most lookups. It also adds `mise bootstrap --upgrade` and `mise env --paths`, and closes a trust gap in remote task files.

## Speed and GitHub API usage

Cold-cache timings for v2026.10.10 versus v2026.10.11, measured with hyperfine on one Linux x64 machine with no GitHub token set:

| Command | v2026.10.10 | v2026.10.11 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mise ls-remote python` | 961 ms | 93 ms |
| `mise install` (jq, ripgrep, fd, bat, gh, shellcheck) | 1.49 s | 1.08 s |
| `mise outdated` (same six tools installed) | 433 ms | 272 ms |

The install and `outdated` runs are noisy (±0.1–0.4s over 4 runs) and the install time includes downloads, so treat them as rough. Requests to `api.github.com` in a cold `mise install` of `github:` tools dropped from 2 to 0. Cold `mise outdated` made 8 network requests before and none now.

- **Public GitHub metadata comes from mise-versions.** With `use_versions_host` on (the default), release lists, `latest`, git tags (aqua `github_tag` packages, ubi and go), artifact attestations (including aqua's `predicate_type` filters) and the digest in the checksum-mismatch hint are read from mise-versions instead of `api.github.com`. GitHub is still asked directly for repositories mise-versions doesn't list when you have a token (the private-repository case), and in paranoid mode for attestations. The direct API is also used with `use_versions_host = false`, GitHub `url_replacements` and custom `api_url`s. [#14460](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14460), [#14461](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14461), [#14469](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14469), [#14481](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14481), [#14477](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14477), [#14443](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14443)
- Other requests also moved off the GitHub API:
  - `mise x`, `mise exec`, shims and `hook-env` use mise-versions when they auto-install a tool. [#14458](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14458)
  - `mise self-update` reads mise's releases from mise-versions and downloads the archive from github.com release downloads. Packslip and zipsign verification are unchanged. [#14464](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14464)
  - `mise lock` downloads artifacts for provenance checks from github.com instead of the API asset endpoint. [#14465](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14465)
  - Aqua registries hosted on GitHub are fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com. [#14470](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14470)
  - Ruby looks up the latest ruby-build release through mise-versions. [#14471](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14471)
- **Fewer version-list fetches.** `mise install`, `use` and `run` now reuse a cached version list for the tool's `minimum_release_age` window minus one hour, clamped to 1–24h. With the default 24h cutoff, that is 23h. `outdated`, `upgrade`, `ls-remote`, `lock` and `latest` still refresh after 1h. If you set `fetch_remote_versions_cache` yourself, your value applies to every command. [#14484](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14484), [#14485](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14485), [#14457](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14457)
- **Faster version resolution:**
  - Multi-tool commands such as `mise outdated` can resolve many registry tools with one request to the mise-versions index. [#14473](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14473)
  - `latest` is resolved without refetching the list. [#14456](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14456)
  - Explicit backend args such as `aqua:jqlang/jq` reuse the registry tool's version list. [#14459](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14459)
  - Release tags come from the versions host instead of being listed or guessed. [#14442](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14442)
  - Packslip installs no longer re-download what resolution already verified. [#14466](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14466)
  - Install tracking and the Python version list are served from static assets. [#14441](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14441)
- **Python version listing no longer clones pyenv.** `mise ls-remote python`, `outdated`, `upgrade` and fuzzy `mise use python@3.12` read the python-build definitions from mise-versions. A cold listing took about 960ms before and about 90ms now. pyenv is still cloned when mise compiles Python, when `python.pyenv_repo` points at a fork, when you're offline, or when `use_versions_host = false`. Some definitions that had no date before now have one, so they are held back by `minimum_release_age` until they are old enough. [#14455](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14455)
- `mise oci build` now requires root for `apt:` packages, as it already did for apk, and fails up front with a clear message. If apt-get still fails, the error now includes the last lines of dpkg's output. [#14447](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14447)
- Registry: `native-sdk` now installs from npm (`@native-sdk/cli`), so the `native` command works. It requires Node 24+. [#14431](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14431)

## Security

- **Remote task files now need trust before their headers render.** A `mise.toml` with only `[tasks]` loads without trust. Before this fix, if one of those tasks set `file` to a remote URL, `mise tasks ls`, `mise tasks info` and `mise tasks validate` rendered the file's `#MISE` headers, so a template like `{{ exec(...) }}` ran without a trust prompt. Remote files now follow the same rule as local task includes: if the headers contain template syntax, the config that references them must be trusted first. Remote files with plain headers still list without trust, and braces in the script body need no trust. [#14416](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14416) (@JamBalaya56562, @risu729)
- Updated rustls to 0.23.46 to address a RustSec advisory. [#14434](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14434)

## Added

- **`mise bootstrap --upgrade`** installs what is missing and then upgrades what is already installed, in a single run. In the packages phase it runs the same upgrade as `mise bootstrap packages upgrade`, and pins are respected. In the tools phase it runs `mise upgrade` without `--bump`, so configured version ranges hold. Both run before the matching post hooks and dependent services. `--dry-run` previews both steps and `--skip` works as before. It does not update mise itself, repositories or images, and it does not restart services. [#14433](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14433)

  ```sh
  mise self-update --yes && mise bootstrap --upgrade
  ```

- **`mise env --paths`** prints the PATH entries mise manages, one per line and in PATH order: tool bin directories, `_.path` entries, and inherited directories that mise moves forward, such as `~/.cargo/bin`. This lets CI integrations export only mise's additions without diffing `PATH`. [#14429](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14429)

  ```console
  $ mise env --paths
  /home/me/.local/share/mise/installs/node/24.11.0/bin
  /home/me/.cargo/bin
  ```

- **The install script downloads pinned versions from mise.jdx.dev.** `curl https://mise.run | MISE_VERSION=<version> sh` now tries mise.jdx.dev first and falls back to GitHub Releases if that download fails. Checksums for pinned versions still come only from GitHub's `SHASUMS256.txt`. If no checksum is found, the script refuses to install. `MISE_INSTALL_FROM_GITHUB=1` still uses GitHub only. [#14446](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14446)
- Registry: `gdal` installs the GDAL/OGR command-line tools from conda-forge (`conda:libgdal-core`). [#14440](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14440) (@ivan-ivkovic)

## Fixed

- **A bare `mise upgrade` no longer installs lazy tools that have never been installed.** Naming the tool still installs it. A lazy tool that already has a version installed upgrades as before. A missing lazy tool is still installed if an upgraded tool depends on it. `mise outdated` now marks these tools as `[MISSING] (lazy)`, and the bare upgrade no longer looks up their versions. [#14422](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14422) (@ryanrhughes), [#14444](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14444)
- Fixed false `stack limit reached` errors on the static musl builds, for example on Ubuntu 26.04. These errors broke aqua `version_filter` parsing and made shims such as kubectl's report "not a valid shim". [#14450](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14450)
- `mise lock --platform ...` run on Alpine or NixOS no longer records Node source builds for other platforms. Only an explicit `node.compile` or `all_compile = true` forces source builds for those targets. [#14432](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14432)
- `mise upgrade --bump` and hand-edited version pins no longer drop a pipx tool's locked uv dependency graph. Before, `mise install --locked` then failed on a fresh checkout. [#14426](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14426) (@wislertt)
- Packslip prefixes such as `fnox@1` now skip releases this host can't install, the same way `latest` does. Each skipped release gets a warning, and if no match can be installed, mise reports a clear error. [#14467](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14467)
- A `bash` shim ahead of `/bin` no longer causes a false "shim fallback recursion detected" error for commands like `bash -c 'bash --version'`. The docs now recommend installing shells with the system package manager instead of `[tools]`. [#14475](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14475)
- Bootstrap UFW rules with an `interface` now render the incoming direction (`ufw allow in on tailscale0 ...`), which fixes `Invalid token 'on'` errors. [#14480](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14480)
- Dotfiles:
  - Before the `files: apply` prompt, mise now lists each file it will create, overwrite or remove and warns that local edits will be replaced. The prompt now defaults to No. [#14430](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14430)
  - `mise dot add --changed` now also captures edited files that a copy-mode `dotfile_groups` root discovers automatically, not just files listed explicitly in `entries`. [#14436](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14436)

## Documentation

- The docs now recommend committing `mise.lock`, so CI and Docker builds skip version lookups. [#14453](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14453)

## New Contributors

* @ivan-ivkovic made their first contribution in [#14440](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14440)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/mise/compare/v2026.10.10...v2026.10.11

## 💚 Sponsor mise

mise is built and maintained by [@jdx](https://github.com/jdx), an open source developer at [**entire.io**](https://entire.io/), the title sponsor of his open source work.

If mise saves you or your team time, please consider becoming an [individual or company sponsor](https://jdx.dev/sponsors.html). Your support funds ongoing development and helps keep mise fast, free, and independent.

name: v2026.10.10: Task skip_if, snap and COPR in bootstrap, and dotfiles pull fixes
body:
Tasks can now skip themselves with a `skip_if` check, and bootstrap gains Snap packages, Fedora COPR repositories, and branch selection for `--adopt`. This release also fixes several `mise dot pull` problems that could loop, stall, or leave sharing paused on long histories. On the Windows side, it fixes `.mise-bins` executables and npm installs restored from a cache.

## Added

- **`skip_if` for tasks.** Before a task runs, mise runs its `skip_if` shell command. If the command exits 0, mise skips the task and counts it as successful. Any other exit status runs the task as usual. [#14399](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14399)

  ```toml
  [tasks.setup]
  skip_if = "test -f .initialized"
  run = "touch .initialized"
  ```

  The check runs after `depends` and before `confirm`. It uses the task's directory, shell, environment, sandbox and `timeout`, and it supports Tera templates and task arguments. Its output is discarded and it gets no stdin. It does not receive the task's `secrets`. File tasks can set it with `#MISE skip_if="..."`. `mise run --force` skips the check, `--dry-run` prints it without running it, and `mise tasks info` shows it. If the check can't start, times out, or is killed, the task fails.

- **Snap packages in bootstrap.** On Linux, you can declare snaps in `[bootstrap.packages]` alongside apt and flatpak, with optional `channel` and `classic`, and `state = "absent"` to remove a snap. If a snap tracks a different channel than you declared, `status` shows it and `apply` moves it with `snap refresh --channel`. snapd can't install or hold a specific version, so `apply` and `upgrade` skip entries with a version pin and print a warning. [#14402](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14402)

  ```toml
  [bootstrap.packages]
  "snap:jq" = "latest"
  "snap:node" = { channel = "22/stable", classic = true }
  ```

- **COPR repositories with `[bootstrap.dnf.repos]`.** You can declare a COPR next to the `dnf:` packages that come from it, instead of using a `pre-packages` hook. mise writes the same `/etc/yum.repos.d` file that `dnf copr enable` does. It does not need the copr plugin, so this also works on Fedora Atomic hosts that layer packages. The chroot is chosen from `/etc/os-release` (Fedora, EL, Amazon Linux). Without `--yes`, mise asks before enabling any COPR. mise never disables or removes repositories, but `mise bootstrap unapply` names any leftover files. [#14401](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14401)

  ```toml
  [bootstrap.dnf.repos]
  ghostty = { copr = "scottames/ghostty" }

  [bootstrap.packages]
  "dnf:ghostty" = "latest"
  ```

- **`mise bootstrap --adopt <url>?ref=<branch>`** adopts a branch other than the default, either for global config or for a setup history. This also works with `mise bootstrap remote`. The ref must be a branch: tags, commits and missing branches are refused before anything is cloned. mise never switches an existing `~/.config/mise` checkout to another branch, even with `--update`, so use `git switch` first. The docs now also explain how `mise dot origin set` relates to an adopted global config. [#14400](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14400)

- **GitHub OAuth refresh token in the Secure Enclave.** On a Mac with Touch ID, set `github.oauth_cache_secure_enclave = true` to keep the native GitHub OAuth refresh token behind Touch ID instead of in plaintext in `github-oauth-tokens.toml`. Touch ID asks for a fingerprint only when the token needs refreshing. If you cancel the prompt, mise skips the refresh and keeps the cached access token. This needs the Developer ID-signed release build. Homebrew and source builds print a warning and keep the token in the cache file. [#14413](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14413)

## Changed

- On Windows, `experimental = true` now turns on the [identity install layout](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/install-layout.html) by itself, which keeps deep npm, pipx and Java trees under the 260-character path limit. Only new installs use it. Existing installs stay where they are, and `mise installs migrate` can move them. To keep the old layout, set `install_layout = "legacy"` (or `MISE_INSTALL_LAYOUT=legacy`). Linux and macOS still need `install_layout = "identity"` set explicitly. [#14392](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14392)

## Fixed

### Dotfiles

- Machines that share an origin and track an encrypted file no longer swap ciphertext back and forth forever. age encryption gives different ciphertext for the same content, so `mise dot watch` could publish commits endlessly without any real edits. Now mise keeps the ciphertext that history already has whenever it decrypts to the same content, mode and recipients. Machines that are already looping settle after one more sync. [#14405](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14405)
- `mise dot pull` on long histories is much faster. The number of git processes no longer grows with the length of the history: in one test with 2,000 commits, a pull went from 137 s to under 6 s. [#14407](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14407), [#14415](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14415)
- When a pull's plan went out of date because another operation saved first, it was treated as a failed apply and paused sharing until someone ran `mise dot pull` by hand. Now, if nothing has been written yet, mise retries on the next attempt and the watcher keeps applying changes. [#14414](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14414)
- After an interrupted history operation, `mise dot pull --yes` no longer fails with "local saved history changed since planning". The pull now recovers the interrupted operation before it plans. [#14410](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14410)
- A file that already has the incoming version (content and mode) is no longer held as an unsaved edit or conflict that pauses sharing. Running `mise dot pull --take-remote <path>` again for a path an earlier pull already resolved no longer fails with "is not a conflict". [#14411](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14411)

### Windows

- `mise x` and shims now run the original executable instead of its copy in `.mise-bins`, for tools installed with aqua `symlink_bins`, github `filter_bins`, or packslip. Programs that look for DLLs or data next to their own executable, such as exiftool, now start correctly. Tools installed by older versions need `mise install --force` to get this. A shell from `mise activate` that finds the copy on `PATH` still runs the copy. [#14397](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14397)
- npm tools installed with the built-in aube installer are reinstalled if their dependency links are missing, for example after a CI cache restore drops NTFS junctions. Before, mise reported them as installed and they failed at run time with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. [#14418](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14418)

### Tools and installs

- `rust@nightly`, `mise ls-remote rust`, and `mise outdated`/`upgrade` now read the nightly manifest from `RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER`, so a mirror such as panamax no longer needs access to `static.rust-lang.org`. If `[env]` sets `RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER` or `RUSTUP_UPDATE_ROOT`, mise also passes them to `rustup-init` and `rustup toolchain install`. [#14384](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14384)
- With a global `minimum_release_age`, `mise use --tool-option minimum_release_age=0s <tool>` now installs the actual latest version instead of the version the global cutoff allows. [#14398](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14398) (@halms)
- Upgrading a global npm tool that `mise lock --global` locked with a dependency graph now regenerates the graph for the new version, including with `--bump`. Before, the upgrade dropped the graph and the next `mise install --locked` failed. [#14419](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14419) (@altendky)
- Reinstalling a packslip tool signed by a shared reusable workflow works again with its saved pin. In v2026.10.9, mise rejected the unchanged signer as "not a workflow of" the tool's repository. Signer, workflow or repository changes are still refused. [#14408](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14408)
- Building Erlang from source now shows `compiling with kerl` while the build runs, instead of staying on `verifying checksum`. kerl's output now prints above the progress row instead of writing over it. [#14391](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14391)
- `mise prune` now shows a progress line while it scans for unused versions, instead of printing nothing for what could be a long time. [#14420](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14420)
- The JSON schema now rejects unknown keys in `env._.python` and its `venv` options, matching what mise already refused at load time. Editors now flag these mistakes. [#14387](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14387) (@JamBalaya56562, @risu729)

## Documentation

- The configuration docs now explain how mise searches for config before listing the per-directory file names. [#14390](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14390)
- The bootstrap overview and run order now include `[bootstrap.apt.sources]`. [#14396](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14396)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/mise/compare/v2026.10.9...v2026.10.10

name: v2026.10.9: path: tool versions require trust; apt repositories, login items and run0/doas in bootstrap
body:
This release fixes a trust bypass: an untrusted `path:` tool version could put a directory on `PATH`. It also adds several bootstrap features: apt repositories and PPAs, macOS login items, rpm-ostree layering on Fedora Atomic, and `run0`/`doas` support. Beyond that, it improves `mise dot status`, adds GitHub OAuth conveniences, and fixes problems across npm, prune, brew and dotfiles sync.

## Security

- **`path:` tool versions now require trust.** Before, an untrusted repository could ship `node path:./local` in `.tool-versions` or `mise.toml`. `mise activate` would then put `./local/bin` ahead of your `PATH` on the next `cd`, without asking for trust, so a `local/bin/git` there would run in place of your real `git`. Configs with a `path:` version are now skipped until trusted, and you see the usual `is not trusted, run mise trust` warning. After `mise trust`, `path:` works as before. Other version forms are unaffected. Reported by Anthropic and Ada Logics. [#14358](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14358)
- `mise bootstrap --adopt` now rejects repository URLs that embed credentials (a `user:TOKEN@` part). It used to quietly fall back to a plain clone, which left the token in `.git/config`. Use a Git credential helper or SSH agent. [#14315](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14315)
- Download file names decoded from URLs (for example `tool%2F..%2Fpwned.tar.gz`, or `C:` names on Windows) can no longer point outside the download directory. Ordinary escapes such as `%20` still decode. [#14274](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14274) (@JamBalaya56562, @hktitof)

## Added

### Bootstrap

- **`[bootstrap.apt.sources]`** declares PPAs and vendor apt repositories next to the packages that come from them. You no longer need a `pre-packages` hook that runs `add-apt-repository`. Each source is written as a deb822 file at `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/mise-<name>.sources`. Its signing key is fetched, trimmed to the fingerprints you declared, and stored inline in that file, so deleting the file removes both the repository and its key. PPAs need only `ppa = "owner/name"` and are added only on Ubuntu and Ubuntu-based distros, so the same config also works on Debian. Other repositories need `uris`, `key` and `fingerprint`; `suites` and `components` are optional. An unpinned `apt:` package that is installed from the distro is moved to the declared source. Inline keys require apt 2.4 or later (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12). [#14306](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14306), [#14348](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14348)

  ```toml
  [bootstrap.apt.sources]
  git-core = { ppa = "git-core/ppa" }
  fish = { ppa = "fish-shell/release-4" }

  [bootstrap.packages]
  "apt:git" = "latest"
  "apt:fish" = "latest"
  ```

- **macOS login items.** `[bootstrap.macos.login_items]` declares the apps listed under "Open at Login". `status` and `plan` report missing apps, and `mise bootstrap` adds them. The list is additive by default, so apps that register themselves are left alone. Set `exclusive = true` to have the config own the whole list. [#14354](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14354)

  ```toml
  [bootstrap.macos.login_items]
  apps = ["/Applications/Ghostty.app", "~/Applications/Example.app"]
  ```

- **Fedora Atomic hosts.** On ostree-booted hosts (Silverblue, Bazzite, secureblue, ...), `dnf:` installs now stop with an explanation instead of failing inside dnf on read-only `/usr`. To layer packages instead, set `system_packages.ostree = "layer"`. mise then runs one `rpm-ostree install` for the whole batch and reports layered packages as `pending reboot` until you reboot. Version pins are skipped, and `upgrade` points you to `rpm-ostree upgrade`. [#14353](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14353), [#14357](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14357)
- **`run0` and `doas` for privilege elevation.** On hosts without `sudo`, mise uses the first of `sudo`, `run0` or `doas` it finds on `PATH`. To always use a specific one, set `system_packages.elevate_with` (or `MISE_SYSTEM_PACKAGES_ELEVATE_WITH`), for example `"run0"`. [#14351](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14351)
- **dnf package groups.** Entries such as `"dnf:@development-tools" = "latest"` are now installed, upgraded and checked as groups. Before, `status` always reported them as missing. Environment groups (`@^name`) are not supported. [#14347](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14347)
- **Templated `[bootstrap.repos]` paths.** Repo keys can use templates, so each machine can choose its own clone location with a var answered once through `mise vars prompt`. Unanswered vars use their `default`. [#14359](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14359)

  ```toml
  [vars.repos_dir]
  default = "~/src"
  prompt = "Where should repositories be cloned?"

  [bootstrap.repos]
  "{{ vars.repos_dir }}/project-a" = { url = "git@github.com:example/project-a.git" }
  ```

### Tools and backends

- **`libc()` and `avx2()` template functions** for `http:` URLs. They let one entry pick `-musl` and no-AVX2 `-baseline` builds: append `{{ avx2(yes="", no="-baseline") }}{{ libc(gnu="", musl="-musl") }}` to the `url` template after `{{ os() }}-{{ arch() }}`. `mise lock` records every variant. [#14298](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14298)
- **PyPI Simple indexes:** when `pypi.registry_url` is not a `/json` URL, mise now asks for the PEP 691 JSON format. If the index supports it, upload times come from the index, so `minimum_release_age` now works with private indexes. HTML-only indexes behave as before. [#14352](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14352)
- **Rust mirrors:** when `RUSTUP_UPDATE_ROOT` is set, `rustup-init` is downloaded from `{root}/dist/<host-triple>/rustup-init` instead of `sh.rustup.rs`. This lets mirrors such as panamax serve the first download too. mise also forwards `RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER` and `RUSTUP_UPDATE_ROOT` from config env to rustup. [#14356](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14356)

### GitHub OAuth

- `github.oauth_copy_code` copies the one-time device code to the clipboard during `mise token github --oauth`, like `gh auth login --clipboard`. When the setting is unset, mise asks in an interactive terminal. Only the device code is copied, never the token. [#14269](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14269)
- `github.oauth_cache_get` and `github.oauth_cache_set` keep the long-lived refresh token in a password manager or keychain, so the plaintext cache file holds only the 8-hour access token. Both settings must be set and can only go in global config. An existing cached refresh token moves into the store at the next refresh. If the store can't be read, mise keeps the cached token. If it can't be written, mise warns and keeps the token in the file. [#14360](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14360)

  ```toml
  [settings.github]
  oauth_cache_get = "pass show mise/github-oauth"
  oauth_cache_set = "pass insert -m -f mise/github-oauth"
  ```

### Dotfiles and skills

- **`mise dot status` output is grouped into sections:** Tracking, Repository, Conflicts, Automatic capture and Bootstrap, followed by a "Next steps" list of commands. The table now lists only entries that need attention and counts the rest. Use `--verbose`/`-v` to list every entry. `--json` and `--missing` are unchanged. [#14361](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14361)
- `mise dot status` now shows tracked entries whose variants don't match this machine as `not on this machine (variants: work)`, instead of plain `tracked`. In `--json`, `state` stays `tracked` and a `reason` field is added. [#14266](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14266)
- `mise skills sync` now lists the skill links it creates, plus `.mise-skills.json`, in the repository's `.git/info/exclude`, so they stay out of `git status`. Your hand-written skills are unaffected, and nothing in the repository itself changes. [#14374](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14374)

## Changed

- **Registry:** `opencode` now installs OpenCode 2 from npm (`npm:@opencode/cli`). `opencode@latest` moves to v2 on your next upgrade. `opencode@1` keeps v1 from aqua. [#14295](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14295)
- **Go:** if `go.mod` or `go.work` has an exact `go X.Y.Z` line and no `toolchain` line, mise now uses it as the toolchain version and no longer shows the deprecation warning. This matches how Go reads the file. The old advice to add a `toolchain` line didn't work, because `go mod tidy` removes it. `go X.Y` lines without a patch version are still deprecated. [#14308](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14308)
- The official `-debian` Docker image now includes `libatomic1`, so Node.js 26 installs and runs without extra steps. [#14303](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14303)

## Fixed

### Tools, shims and updates

- `auto_update` now updates only tools that are already installed. Since 2026.10.7, the first shell prompt could install every lazy tool declared with `auto_update`. [#14368](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14368) (@ryanrhughes)
- Downloads started by `mise exec`, `mise x` and shims now retry up to `http_retries`, like `mise install`. Before, they made a single attempt. Remote version lookups still make one attempt, so shims don't get slower. [#14342](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14342)
- npm tools installed from a lockfile in one project no longer show up as missing, or as `<version>~aube~<digest>`, in another config that requests `latest` or a version prefix without a lockfile. With `install_layout = "identity"`, unlocked requests get their own plain install, separate from the project's lockfile-built one. The same applies to uv-locked pipx tools. [#14307](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14307), [#14309](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14309)
- `mise prune` no longer removes tool versions used only by inline task `tools`. It also keeps a uv-locked `pipx:`/`pypi:` tool's installs for every Python version, not just the one in the current directory. [#14334](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14334), [#14335](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14335)
- Running reshim in one project no longer deletes `[wrappers]` command wrappers defined in other projects. [#14355](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14355)
- With `skills.auto_sync`, `mise upgrade` now relinks agent skills to the new version. Before, the links kept pointing at the replaced install, which `prune` could then delete. [#14373](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14373)
- Remote tasks no longer break commits when they are fetched from a git hook. Their clone was writing over the commit's index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`). Fixed by updating gix to 0.89. [#14316](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14316) (@any-victor)
- Packslip tools whose signing workflow moved, such as aube moving from `release-plz.yml` to `release.yml`, now upgrade when both workflows are in the `workflow` list. `mise lock` also keeps the signer of a renamed or transferred project. [#14338](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14338), [#14362](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14362)
- aqua packages that have no repo now print the "cannot list versions" warning once, and it tells you to pin an exact version. [#14336](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14336)
- On Windows, the `tool-update` service no longer opens a console window that stops the updater when you close it. [#14344](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14344)

### Homebrew and system packages

- Brew bottles now install their `etc`/`var` files and run the formula's `post_install_steps`. For example, `openssl@4` now gets its CA bundle and `openssl.cnf`. Existing files are kept, and the bottle's copy is saved next to them as `.default`. Protected `copy` steps (`overwrite: false`) are respected. [#14272](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14272), [#14311](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14311)
- On Linux, Homebrew `uses_from_macos` dependencies are now installed. This fixes runtime errors such as `libbz2.so.1.0` missing for `brew:chafa`. [#14288](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14288) (@itskyf)
- `mise bootstrap` no longer runs `chown` on a Homebrew prefix owned by another non-root user. It stops with an explanation instead. [#14345](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14345)
- Casks that mise evaluates itself now support the `generate_completions_from_executable` stanza. [#14255](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14255) (@pmmmwh)
- `mise oci build` no longer runs the host's apt hooks against the image. Those hooks broke non-root builds that install packages such as `cmake`. [#14296](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14296)
- When elevation is unavailable, mise no longer tells you to run privileged helpers that read their plan from stdin, because they can't run on their own. It now tells you to re-run the mise command as root. [#14350](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14350)

### Dotfiles

- When another machine had saved a profile-variant file while that profile was inactive here, turning the profile on no longer publishes a deletion or reverts the shared file. Status reports it as `not applied here`, and `mise dot pull` applies it, or stops with a conflict that you resolve with `--take-remote` or `--keep-local`. [#14275](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14275)
- After `mise bootstrap --adopt`, unchanged encrypted files reuse the ciphertext already in history. Before, they were re-encrypted, and `mise dot sync` paused on a conflict. [#14300](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14300)
- When `/home` is a symlink (Fedora Atomic), adopting now restores `config/` entries, and `mise dot origin set` no longer shows a false "Not portable" warning. [#14315](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14315)
- `mise dot apply` applies entries that write mise's own config first, then plans everything else from the new config. A newly added entry now takes effect in a single run. [#14339](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14339)
- `mise dot diff` now shows per-file hunks, missing files and type mismatches for directory copy entries. [#14333](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14333)

### Schema

- The JSON schema now accepts `[bootstrap.secrets]`, `[bootstrap.groups]`, `[bootstrap.users]`, and table forms of `vars._.file` and `vars._.source`. Editors and linters such as tombi and Taplo no longer flag configs that mise accepts. [#14322](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14322), [#14340](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14340), [#14383](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14383) (@JamBalaya56562, @risu729)

## Documentation

- New guidance on when to use `mise bootstrap --from` versus `--adopt`, why `fish = "auto"` is recommended for fish activation, when to use `mise dot sync`, `pull` and `apply`, and how to check from a shim whether a tool is installed. [#14301](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14301), [#14304](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14304), [#14343](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14343), [#14337](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14337)

## Upgrade notes

- If an untrusted project uses a `path:` tool version, run `mise trust` in it.
- Scripts that parse the default table from `mise dot status` should add `--verbose` or switch to `--json`.
- `opencode@latest` moves to OpenCode 2. Pin `opencode@1` to stay on v1.
- `mise bootstrap --adopt` with a URL that contains credentials now fails. Use a credential helper or SSH agent instead.

## Registry

- New aqua packages: [`Alice39s/xmtr`](https://github.com/Alice39s/xmtr), [`bufbuild/protoschema-plugins/protoc-gen-jsonschema`](https://github.com/bufbuild/protoschema-plugins) and [`takumin/qemu-bin`](https://github.com/takumin/qemu-bin).

## New Contributors

* @pmmmwh made their first contribution in [#14255](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14255)
* @itskyf made their first contribution in [#14288](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14288)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/mise/compare/v2026.10.8...v2026.10.9

If mise saves you or your team time, please consider becoming an [individual or company sponsor](https://jdx.dev/sponsors.html). Your support funds ongoing development and helps keep mise fast, free, and independent.

name: v2026.10.8: Stable `global` install link for IDEs
body:
Each tool's install directory now has a `global` link that follows your global config, which gives IDEs a path that doesn't change when you switch versions. This release also retries downloads whose response body drops partway through, fixes lockfile checks for release tags that contain `@`, and stops dotfiles history from rewriting files that haven't changed.

## Added

- **`global` runtime symlink.** Each tool's install directory now has a `global` link to the version your global and system config select. Programs that can't run mise, such as IDEs, can point at this path and follow `mise use -g` changes. [#14271](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14271)

  ```text
  ~/.local/share/mise/installs/maven/
  ├── 3.9.13/
  ├── 3.9.16/
  └── global -> ./3.9.16
  ```

  The link is updated along with the other runtime symlinks (`latest`, `3`, ...), for example after `mise use -g`, `mise install` and `mise upgrade`. Project config and `MISE_*_VERSION` don't change it. If no global config selects the tool, mise removes the link. A real directory named `global` is left alone. The link is always on, and no setting turns it off.

## Fixed

- HTTP requests now retry, up to `http_retries`, when the response body drops partway through. Before, only the request and headers were retried, so a version list or release page cut off mid-transfer failed with `error decoding response body`. This applies to text, JSON and byte requests, and to version lists read with `version_regex`. [#14253](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14253) (@JamBalaya56562)
- `mise install` no longer rejects lockfile entries whose release tag contains `@`, such as `cli@0.46.0`. `mise lock` writes these tags percent-encoded (`cli%400.46.0`), and the locked-URL check read that as version `400.46.0`. Re-running `mise lock` couldn't fix it. [#14252](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14252)
- Dotfiles history index rebuilds now skip checkpoint metadata files whose contents haven't changed. On large histories, rebuilds used to rewrite every file, which caused minutes of disk writes and made `mise dot save` fail with `another history operation is running`. [#14249](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14249)
- The JSON schema now accepts `outputs = { auto = false }` on tasks, so editors and linters such as tombi and Taplo no longer flag it. mise's behavior is unchanged: `auto = false` means the same as leaving `outputs` unset. [#14265](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14265) (@JamBalaya56562)

## Documentation

- The dotfiles docs now open with a recommended setup, and the modes-and-keys reference table has been reorganized into three readable columns. [#14267](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14267)

## Registry

- New aqua packages: [`runxhq/runx`](https://github.com/runxhq/runx) and [`takumin/passt-bin`](https://github.com/takumin/passt-bin).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/mise/compare/v2026.10.7...v2026.10.8
